messages:
kyle-runtime: Heads-up — proposing a small rework of the batcher ownership boundaries. TL;DR: move slot ownership out of the coalescer and into the admission layer to simplify preemptions and make eviction signals deterministic.

kyle-runtime: Current problem: coalescer owns slots + does admission shaping. When we preempt, we end up with racy slot handoffs and lots of tail latency. Hard to reason about lease timeouts.

omar-ml: Curious — moving ownership to admission sounds promising for determinism. How do you intend to handle hot tenants that want steady low latency?

kyle-runtime: Good q. Proposal sketch: admission will hold lightweight "slot leases" that define headroom and eviction priority. Coalescer becomes purely a packing/shape optimiser (no long-lived ownership). Hot tenants get reserved slots via long leases; bursty ones get short leases + backoff.

jen-product: From product side: we need an easy knob to guarantee p95 latency for Dedicated customers. Does this change make guarantees easier?

kyle-runtime: Yes — separating concerns lets us map SLAs to admission lease policies. We can offer a "p95 reservation" that maps to N reserved slots + strict preemption weight. Less jitter in coalescer packing as it no longer decides eviction.

Tina-sre: Concern: state transitions. Where do we persist lease metadata? In-memory will be simpler, but cross-node rebalances need consistent view.

kyle-runtime: Plan: lease table in the runtime control plane with ephemeral local caches. Control plane writes are authoritative; nodes subscribe to delta streams. Local caches have TTL + conflict resolution by versioned leases.

Tina-sre: Sounds fine but we must be explicit about failure modes: control plane partition => nodes continue with last-known leases and degrade gracefully. Add a safety TTL so leases expire if heartbeats stop.

omar-ml: Another ML angle — KV cache affinity. If admission moves slots, we need a fast signal to evict/transfer KV caches or warm up replicas. Otherwise inference costs spike.

kyle-runtime: Agreed. Proposal includes a lightweight transfer protocol: admission emits a "handoff intent" event with (slot_id, src_node, dst_node, sequence). Receiver can prefetch KV ranges. Small code sketch: 
```
// pseudo-event
{
  type: "lease_transfer",
  slot: "s-123",
  from: "node-a",
  to: "node-b",
  seq: 42
}
```

jen-product: Will this add visible latency for callers during transfer?

kyle-runtime: It shouldn't for long leases — we plan prefix caching + mirrored KV for a short overlap window. For short leases we accept minimal extra 10-30ms for edge cases; can tune later.

Tina-sre: Observability checklist: lease acquisition/release events, transfer latency, KV warmup hit rate, preemption counts, and drop-reason histogram. Tag by tenant, model, and route.

omar-ml: Also expose a metric for "kvcache-miss-cost" so Optimize can recommend reservation changes automatically.

ci-bot: pipeline status: batcher-ownership-proto branch passed unit tests (15/15), integration pipeline queued. :white_check_mark:

kyle-runtime: Next steps: I'll open an RFC doc with the sequence diagrams, failure cases, and a small simulation (1000 tenants, mixed qps) to show latency tail improvements. Can folks review tomorrow?

jen-product: Yep — I can do a product impact pass.

Tina-sre: I can work up the observability and runbook bits.

omar-ml: Happy to review the KV warmup logic and simulation inputs.

kyle-runtime: Thanks all — I'll drop the RFC link here when it's ready. :coffee:
